A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRoP research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renamed sections and relocated analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations and image-classification experiments, including pruning, class robustness, imbalanced-data and Waterbirds evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds Wide-ResNet-101 results and Waterbirds analyses. Its empirical evidence is not limited to the newly quoted results from other work.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains validation-error-based class quotas, saturation handling and random sampling within classes. The added Wide-ResNet architecture is an evaluation configuration, not a revision to the proposed pruning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, ImageNet, Waterbirds and Gaussian-mixture simulations, including the existing imbalanced-data and group-robustness scenarios. The larger model and additional Waterbirds analyses do not introduce new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Waterbirds Figure 9 substantially broadens the comparison beyond pruning methods and CDB-W by adding LfF, JTT, Learning to Split, XRM and Bias Amplification. These methods participate as plotted comparison points; their scores are imported from published results rather than established as new runs by this work.

E3.justification: v4 adds a Wide-ResNet-101/CIFAR-100 configuration with 200 training epochs and learning-rate drops at 60/120/160 (Table 1). Waterbirds reporting extends to density 0.1 and includes ordinary per-example test accuracy alongside training-proportion-weighted accuracy (Figure 15). Existing splits, preprocessing and model configurations are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds a larger-model applicability check (Appendix D, Figure 13) and examines Waterbirds accuracy weighting, retained group sizes and group performance at density 0.1 (Appendix F, Figure 15). The existing pre-training-length ablation and class-wise analyses are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed averages with min/max bands for pruning comparisons, five-seed averaging for EL2N/GraNd scores and ten datasets for the Gaussian simulation. The added Wide-ResNet experiment follows the existing reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v4 adds results showing continued DRoP robustness benefits with Wide-ResNet-101, lower-density Waterbirds results, imported baseline scores and alternative-accuracy/group breakdowns. Most existing curves remain unchanged, and Table 2 largely tabulates existing comparisons. That table reports 45.3% worst-class accuracy for Random+DRoP on half of CIFAR-100, while both versions' main text gives 45.4%; this is an unresolved reporting discrepancy, not an established performance change.

T1.justification: The Gaussian-mixture definitions, optimal-prior derivations, Theorem B.1, Lemma B.2, SSP analysis and multivariate isotropic extension are unchanged. Section renumbering and equation reflow do not alter the mathematical arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the same central claims: existing pruning can exacerbate classification bias, Gaussian analysis motivates class quotas, and DRoP combines robustness improvements with data reduction. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 explains the Waterbirds weighted-average decline through DRoP's retention of minority groups at the expense of heavily weighted majority groups, and contrasts ordinary test accuracy. It also discusses effectiveness with a stronger full-data model and competitiveness with additional robustness methods. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly supplies a code-repository link and the added Wide-ResNet configuration. Appendices A/D describe its expansion factor and removal of early downsampling layers. Appendix F documents Waterbirds accuracy weighting and test-group counts; these disclosures do not establish changes to the original data split.

R1.justification: v4 adds targeted references for Waterbirds robustness competitors and their reported scores, model-size robustness and Wide-ResNet. These extend the empirical positioning, while the broader related-work discussion and novelty claims remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 separates Related Work from a numbered Data Pruning Is Not Robust section, reorganizes the final appendices and adds localized explanatory passages. The title gains 'Data', the publication header changes and acknowledgements are added; most existing prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds numerical Table 2 and figures for the larger-model and Waterbirds analyses, extends Table 1 and revises Figure 9's axes and baseline legend. The first two figures exchange order and appendix figures move, while most existing graphical content is retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens validation through the larger-model check and broader Waterbirds comparison. The weighting analysis clarifies an otherwise ambiguous accuracy trade-off, and the code link and numerical table improve reproducibility information and readability. Imported comparator scores provide less assurance than controlled reruns, and Table 2 introduces the small 45.3% versus 45.4% inconsistency, but these limitations do not outweigh the incremental gains.
